How to Read Your Dog's Poop (Firmness and Color)

The ideal poop is brown and firm, a good, well-formed poop. If changes in color or firmness last more than a few days, talk to your vet.

General guide to firmness

StateWhat it may mean (common guidelines)
Too hardPossible constipation. Check water intake and activity.
Firm (Good)Often described as healthy
SoftMay point to indigestion, stress or a diet change
Fully liquid (diarrhea)Risk of dehydration. See a vet if it lasts more than a day.

General guide to color

ColorWhat it may mean (common guidelines)
BrownOften described as normal
GreenishMay have eaten a lot of grass
Dark red · bloodyCan be an emergency sign. See a vet right away.
White · grayPossible bile or liver issue. A vet visit is recommended.
These tables are general reference information, not a diagnosis. If you notice anything unusual, always check with your vet.

Why it helps to log it with POOPIEMATE

When you log a poop in POOPIEMATE, you can also note its state: Good (well-formed), Loose or Hard. Once you have a record of the usual pattern, you can tell your vet exactly "when it started and how it changed" if something shifts.

Log poop condition with POOPIEMATE

FAQ

What does a "good" poop look like?

A brown poop that's firm enough to hold its shape is generally what people call a good, well-formed poop.

What should I do if I see bloody or black poop?

Bloody, dark red, or white or gray poop can be an emergency sign, so we recommend seeing a vet right away.
